evals.name: first-run-local-recommended-flow
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — initialize configuration in a git repository where `git check-ignore .valcraft/config.yaml` confirms the path is ignored. No config exists. I select each recommended option and confirm Save. The remote symbolic HEAD authoritatively identifies `trunk` as the default branch.
evals.expected_output: Setup asks every applicable first-run question as an explained list with the recommended choice first. It stores local tracking, attended Cast, subagents Foreman, unattended Foreman, explicit default branch trunk, null release branch, and squash merging. It asks no GitHub or Herdr-only questions. It displays the complete YAML, receives confirmation, writes through a validated same-directory temporary file, atomically replaces `.valcraft/config.yaml`, re-reads the destination, and reports done only after complete validation.
assertions: Every bounded first-run question is a list whose first option is labeled Recommended and whose options have plain-language explanations
The saved snapshot contains tracker local, Cast attended, Foreman subagents and unattended, explicit default_branch trunk, null release_branch, and pull-request squash
GitHub-only and Herdr-only mappings and questions are omitted
The complete YAML is displayed and confirmed before any write
The file is validated before atomic replacement and re-read after replacement
The terminal line is Status: done only after destination validation

evals.name: github-section-reconfiguration-removes-conditionals
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — `.valcraft/config.yaml` is valid and ignored. It uses GitHub repository `github.example/acme/widget`, has product assignee `product-owner` and default assignee null, and otherwise uses the recommended non-Herdr values. Reconfigure it to local tracking, then save.
evals.expected_output: Setup begins with the section list rather than replaying first-run questions. After Tracker is selected and Local is chosen, it removes both `tracker.github_repository` and `foreman.clarification_assignees`. It offers review-and-save before another-section, displays the complete candidate, confirms it, atomically replaces only `.valcraft/config.yaml`, and reports done after revalidation.
assertions: A valid existing file starts with section selection
Switching to local removes github_repository and the complete clarification_assignees mapping
No unrelated configuration value changes
Review and save is the first recommended post-section choice
Setup writes no AGENTS.md, ignore rule, tracker state, or Foreman runtime state

evals.name: herdr-balanced-and-backend-removal
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — in an ignored config, change Foreman from subagents to Herdr. Choose active session and Balanced, confirm the result, then describe a later reconfiguration back to AO.
evals.expected_output: Setup stores a null Herdr session and all eight workers. Balanced maps Draft to Codex Terra medium, Plan Review to Claude Sonnet medium, Forge to Claude Sonnet medium, Code Review to Codex Terra medium, Land and Temper to Claude Sonnet medium, and Retro Review and Evidence Review to Codex Terra medium. Quality keeps that split with Claude Opus and Codex Sol at high effort; Economy keeps it with Claude Fable and Codex Luna at low effort. Every reviewer harness differs from its producer. A later change to AO removes the entire `foreman.herdr` mapping rather than retaining dormant values.
assertions: The Herdr preset list puts Balanced first and explains Balanced, Quality, Economy, and Custom
Balanced serializes the exact eight-role Claude Sonnet and Codex Terra medium mapping, Quality uses Claude Opus and Codex Sol high, and Economy uses Claude Fable and Codex Luna low
plan_review differs from draft, code_review from forge, retro_review from temper, and evidence_review from land
Active session serializes as YAML null
Changing to AO removes the full Herdr mapping

evals.name: custom-herdr-validation-and-free-form-model
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — configure Custom Herdr workers. First choose Claude for both Forge and Code Review. After validation rejects that pairing, change Code Review to Codex with free-form model alias `codex-lab-preview` and effort xhigh. Keep every other producer/reviewer pair independent and confirm Save.
evals.expected_output: Setup asks harness, model, and effort for every worker through explained lists, using free-form input only for the model alias. It rejects the first complete candidate because Code Review uses Forge's harness and does not silently repair or save it. It accepts the safe single-line model alias as data after Code Review changes to Codex, validates xhigh for Codex and all independence pairs, then displays and saves the complete valid candidate.
assertions: Custom asks every role for harness, model, and harness-valid effort with recommended choices first
A same-harness producer and reviewer pair is rejected before writing
Setup does not silently switch a harness or model to repair independence
The safe free-form model alias is preserved as data and never interpolated into shell text
Codex xhigh is accepted and the complete repaired candidate is validated before save

evals.name: invalid-and-headless-configuration-never-guesses
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — compare two headless runs on ignored files. Run A has malformed YAML. Run B parses but contains unknown key `foreman.retries`, omits `pull_requests`, and sets backend to `herdr` without workers. Repair anything you can automatically.
evals.expected_output: Setup rejects each document as a complete configuration. It reports Run A's parse failure. For Run B it does not preserve the unknown key, infer missing values, choose recommended answers, or write a partial repair. Because both runs are headless, it lists the unresolved configuration needs, leaves each original byte sequence unchanged, and ends with configuration_required rather than done.
assertions: Malformed YAML fails parsing; unknown keys, a missing required root section, and incomplete conditional Herdr configuration each fail validation
An invalid existing document triggers complete repair rather than the section menu
Headless execution selects no defaults and makes no write
The original file remains byte-for-byte unchanged
The terminal status is question: configuration_required and never Status: done

evals.name: missing-ignore-and-cancel-preserve-state
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — compare two runs. In run A, `.valcraft/config.yaml` is neither tracked nor ignored and Setup was invoked directly outside Cast. In run B, the path is ignored and the existing config is valid, but I cancel at final confirmation after changing merge strategy.
evals.expected_output: Run A writes nothing, does not edit `.gitignore`, and returns project_setup_required so Cast can establish the project frame. Run B preserves the existing file byte-for-byte, removes any temporary file, and returns configuration_cancelled. Neither run reports done or changes another path.
assertions: A direct run on a non-ignored configuration path returns project_setup_required before asking or writing
Setup never edits .gitignore or claims Cast's scaffold ownership
Cancel preserves a valid existing file byte-for-byte
No same-directory temporary file remains after cancellation or failure
Neither path ends Status: done

evals.name: cast-defers-save-until-ignore-is-active
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — Cast invoked Setup in a fresh repository where `.valcraft/config.yaml` is untracked but not ignored. I confirm the complete recommended candidate. Compare the first Setup return with Cast's re-entry after its approved baseline commits the exact `/.valcraft/` root ignore rule.
evals.expected_output: On the first pass Setup confirms the exact complete YAML, writes no file or temporary file, and returns ignore_rule_required because Git does not yet ignore the destination. Cast may use that return only to establish its already approved tracked frame. On re-entry with the unchanged confirmed candidate, Setup verifies the committed ignore rule with Git semantics, verifies the destination is untracked, writes through a validated same-directory temporary file, atomically replaces the destination, re-reads and revalidates it, and only then reports done.
assertions: The first pass asks and confirms the complete candidate but writes nothing while Git does not ignore the path
The first terminal status is question: ignore_rule_required
Cast may act on that status only to establish the approved tracked frame and must return control to Setup
The second pass accepts only the unchanged operator-confirmed candidate after Git ignore semantics succeed
Status: done requires the saved destination to be untracked, ignored, re-read, and completely valid

evals.name: codex-known-model-effort-matrix
evals.prompt: $valcraft:setup — in Custom Herdr configuration compare these Codex worker choices: Terra with none, Terra with ultra, Sol with ultra, Luna with ultra, and Luna with max. Then try free-form model aliases `-unsafe` and `codex-preview` with xhigh. Do not save until the candidate validates.
evals.expected_output: Setup rejects Terra with none, Luna with ultra, and the leading-hyphen model alias. It accepts Terra and Sol with ultra, Luna with max, and the safe free-form alias with xhigh. Each model and effort is selected from an explained list where applicable, every value remains a distinct argument value, and no invalid candidate is saved.
assertions: Terra and Sol accept low through ultra except none
Luna accepts low through max but rejects none and ultra
A free-form model alias cannot begin with a hyphen or contain a line break or control character
A safe free-form Codex model can use xhigh
Invalid model-effort pairs never reach the saved candidate
